findings.reason: the author should either cite the real precedent (the `deferred` section classification in `plan_executable_remainder`, _schema.py:812) or state plainly that removing a terminal non-shipped plan is a new rule, because modelling a new rule on a precedent that does not exist is exactly the silent fork the rubric exists to catch.
findings.text: §4's stated repair models the new rule on an existing one ("a terminal non-shipped member leaves the denominator the way a deferred one does"), but no deferred member leaves the closure denominator today: `resolve_graph_target` builds `total = len(member_keys)` from every reachable member (roadmap.py:1850,1922) and a schedule-deferred member is reported only through `schedule_override` while still counted in `completion.total` (tests/test_graph_target.py:195-225, `completion == {"shipped": 2, "total": 4}`) — so the cited precedent is absent and the rule §4 proposes is new

findings.reason: repairing one and not the others reproduces the plan's own measured defect one surface over (the exact failure §3's landed comment records, where the field landed on `immediate_roadmap` and `ready_now` got nothing), so the plan must name the owning function to extend and state whether the other two are covered or deliberately excluded.
findings.text: §4's done-when says "a completion figure" singular but names no owner, while closure completion is computed independently three times: `shipped_of_total` in `resolve_graph_target` (roadmap.py:1852/1922, the graph ship-target read), `shipped_fraction` in `_dependency_endpoints` (roadmap.py:2076/2101, surfaced as the `endpoints` array via mcp_views.py:1135 and serve.py:2014), and `lifecycle_completion_pct` in `_north_star_rows` (roadmap.py:525/531) — all three cap below 100% for a terminal non-shipped member

findings.reason: the design must name `plan_section_anchors` as the identity source to extend (reading `section_declarations` and authored section ids) rather than adding a parallel resolver inside the closure walk, and must record the anchor repair as a dependency of the membership change — otherwise the new membership resolves against the same incomplete section set and the feature stays as unusable as the abandoned `gs-absolute-accuracy-gates#s3` ref that motivated it.
findings.text: the §4 option "a stage-scoped dependency resolves membership to the section" proposes a new section-membership resolution, but section identity already has an owner that §4's own evidence comment identifies as broken: `plan_section_anchors` (_schema.py:754) derives a plan's sections from gate sections and comment keys only, ignoring authored `<h2 id>` and `section_declarations` (the same comment records 13 plans carrying declared sections the validator cannot see)

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §4's denominator change is a single predicate inside the existing closure walk (`resolve_graph_target`), not a spread of shallow wrappers over it.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §4 names no owner for "a completion figure", and the codebase computes closure/North-Star completion independently in three places that a repair must reconcile.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §2 and §3 reuse the existing closure machinery well (`_dependency_endpoints`, `TERMINAL_STATUSES`, `is_section_scoped`), but §4 builds its repair on a precedent ("the way a deferred one does") that the closure denominator does not implement.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §2/§3 extend the existing readers in place (`_dependency_endpoints`, `build_roadmap`) rather than adding a parallel layer, and nothing proposed is a forward-only wrapper.
